predecessors.name: Pala Empire
predecessors.text: east Bengal (Vanga), as the pala-empire dossier's loss of 1072 draws it

predecessors.name: Chandra dynasty
predecessors.text: Vanga round Bikrampur, 25 km south of Dhaka

successors.name: Sena dynasty
successors.text: southeastern Bengal (Vanga), ousted from the Varmans (the sena-dynasty dossier's region)

ledger.x: c. 1152: Vijayasena ousts the Varmans from southeastern Bengal. 'So it seems probable that Vijaya Sena ousted the Varmans from southeastern Bengal in the middle of the 12th century AD'; the Varman infobox says 'disestablished 1150 A.D'. Mirror of sena-dynasty ledger 3 (c. 1152), whose region is…

c. 1152: the Varman rule of southeast Bengal ends. 'Bhojavarman was defeated by Vijaysena of Sena dynasty and rule of Varmans over southeast Bengal came to an end'; 'the Belava plate was issued in his fifth regnal year'. The page gives no year; infobox 1150.

wars.name: Jatavarman's campaigns
wars.outcome: Jatavarman 'attacked Varendra with a hostility towards Buddhism' (part of the Somapura monastery was burned), 'snatched away a part of Pundravardhana, then under the sovereign rule of Kamarupa' and 'must have involved him in a struggle with the Pala Empire'…

wars.name: Sena conquest of Vanga
wars.outcome: Bhojavarman defeated by Vijayasena; the Varmans lose southeastern Bengal 'in the middle of the 12th century'.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the extent is the pala-empire dossier's reading.
